report.title: RAG Human Annotation Analysis Framework
report.research_question: RQ-RAG-HUMAN: How do expert human evaluators rate generated RAG responses on factual correctness, evidence grounding, citation validity, and pedagogical clarity across English, Telugu, and code-mixed settings?
report.hypothesis: IndicLearn generated responses achieve mean factual correctness and evidence support >= 4.0/5.0 with quadratic weighted Cohen's kappa >= 0.60 across independent expert annotators.
report.procedure: Independent double-annotation of RAG responses against retrieved course evidence chunks using 7 explicit 5-point Likert rating dimensions with strict anti-hallucination guidelines.

report.interpretation: The RAG human evaluation framework is verified and operational. Because no human annotators have been recruited yet, zero ratings or agreement scores are manufactured. Analysis pipeline is primed for immediate execution upon annotator data submission.
scientific_claims: The evaluation pipeline establishes complete statistical and inter-rater agreement analysis for human RAG evaluation without data fabrication.
limitations: Automated computational metrics (EXP-005A, EXP-005B) do not replace human judgment of pedagogical correctness.
High inter-rater agreement does not guarantee factual ground truth; expert calibration is essential.
Final empirical claims require recruiting qualified bilingual engineering evaluators.
